summary: Intermittent 5xx surge during high-volume batch + streaming fan-out causing request failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat reports an increase in 5xx error rate for production requests that use large batch submissions with streaming fan-out to multiple sub-requests (chat + retrieval + reranking). Errors began ~2026-03-10T08:05Z and recur under high batch+stream concurrency. Affects dedicated pool in us-east-1.

Impact:
- ~8-12% of batch requests return 5xx on affected endpoints during peak bursts.
- Customer reports user-facing errors and retries causing cost spikes.
- No data loss reported; failures are transient but frequent enough to disrupt service.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-03-10 08:05Z: BrightChat first reports increased failures.
- 2026-03-10 08:12Z: Support triaged and escalated to SRE; initial mitigation to throttle per-route burst.
- 2026-03-10 09:00Z: SRE observed correlated autoscaler events + serving-runtime restarts.
- 2026-03-11 02:30Z: Added temporary routing fallback to smaller model variant for heavy fanouts.

Observed behavior and error signals:
- HTTP 503 / 502 returned from API gateway and from upstream serving-runtime.
- Serving runtime logs show "worker OOM" and "connection reset by peer" on some request shards.
- Autoscaler shows frequent scale-up then immediate scale-down cycles during bursts (thrashing).
- KV-cache miss rate spikes during fanout; cache thrash inferred.

Why this ticket is different from past 5xx spikes:
- Failures strongly correlate with combined pattern: large batch sizes + streaming fan-out to multiple downstream tasks (retrieval, rerank).
- Not a pure GPU overload—some nodes show low GPU utilization but high CPU and IO for worker coordination and cache activity.

Current severity: customer-impacting (P1 / Sev1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit a single batch request that contains 80 conversations (or >5000 total tokens) with streaming enabled.
2) For each conversation, the pipeline triggers retrieval and reranking sub-requests simultaneously (fan-out of ~4 sub-requests per conversation).
3) Repeat with concurrency of 20 simultaneous batch requests from a single client at peak time.

Expected: Stable responses with occasional tail latency.
Observed: Elevated 5xx rate, intermittent upstream disconnects and worker restarts.

investigation_notes: 03/10 08:30 SRE (Rohan): Verified pattern reproduces in internal staging with similar batch+fanout. Identified worker OOM traces that align to shard handling code path for rerank step.
03/10 09:15 Eng (S. Liu): Observed per-shard memory allocation spikes when streaming + multiple sub-requests are active; per-request coordination increases pinned CPU and socket usage.

03/10 10:00 SRE: Autoscaler aggressive cooldown config allows quick scale-up but scales down when small number of nodes appear idle (thrash). Buffering/backpressure not applied to fan-out sub-requests causing many concurrent shards to land on few workers.
03/11 02:40 Support: Applied routing policy to send heavy fanout routes to a dedicated smaller-model pool; observed immediate drop in 5xx to ~1.2%.

Hypotheses: (a) Combination of high per-shard memory + coordination overhead causes workers to hit OOM or reset connection; (b) Autoscaler thrash amplifies transient overload by removing capacity before shards fully finish; (c) KV-cache thrash increases IO and CPU, exacerbating worker instability.

Next tests proposed: Increase per-worker memory limit in a canary pool; apply backpressure at gateway to cap concurrent fanout per-request; increase autoscaler stabilization window to avoid immediate scale-downs.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:14 - Support (Ava): Received initial customer report. Asked for request ids and sample payloads. Customer provided 4 failing request ids and logs.
2026-03-10 08:22 - SRE (Rohan): Triage started. Noted OOM traces in runtime logs; escalating to runtime team. Added priority P1.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Eng (S. Liu): Confirmed reproduction in staging with large batch + retrieval+rerank. Working on a small fix to the shard allocation code; will run canary.
2026-03-10 09:45 - Support (Ava): Communicated temporary guidance to customer to reduce batch size to 30 per request and disable streaming as workaround; customer agreed to test.
2026-03-11 03:00 - SRE (Rohan): Rolled out autoscaler cooldown increase on a canary pool (stabilization from 60s -> 300s). Observed reduced thrash and lower 5xx for canary routes.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Customer (BrightChat - ops): Reported that applying suggested changes reduced errors to acceptable levels; requested ETA for permanent fix and guidance for production traffic shaping.
resolution:
Partial mitigation applied: routing heavy fanout routes to a dedicated smaller-model pool and increasing autoscaler stabilization window for canary pool. Customer advised to reduce batch size and disable streaming for highest fanout cases as immediate workaround.

Planned next steps:
- Runtime team to land guardrails for per-shard memory accounting and connection handling (PR #842 under review).
- Autoscaler config change to be rolled to all dedicated pools after validation (target: 2026-03-15).
- Add gateway-level soft backpressure counter to cap concurrent fanout per request.
- Follow-up runbook update and postmortem to be drafted in Confluence.
